title: Query Process Runs
---

# Query Process Runs

Process-run queries support process-template filters, typed parameter filters,
relationship inclusion, visibility, ordering, and pagination.

## Filter process templates

Use `filter()` for query fields and `Field` predicates for portable structured
comparisons.

```python
from recap.dsl.query import Field

runs = (
    namespace.query_maker()
    .process_runs()
    .where(Field("process_template.name") == "Collect")
    .where(Field("name").starts_with("Run-"))
    .all()
)
```

## Filter parameters

`filter_parameter()` requires exactly one comparator. Use `eq`, range
comparators, `between`, or membership with `in_`; pass `step` when parameter
names repeat across steps.

```python
query = namespace.query_maker()

exact = query.process_runs().filter_parameter(
    "detector", eq="pilatus", step="Collect"
).all()

in_range = query.process_runs().filter_parameter(
    "exposure", between=(0.1, 1.0), step="Collect"
).all()

selected = query.process_runs().filter_parameter(
    "energy", in_=[8.0, 12.0, 16.0], value_type="float"
).all()
```

## Include run relationships

```python
runs = (
    query.process_runs()
    .include_steps(include_parameters=True)
    .include_resources()
    .all()
)
```

`include_steps()` loads steps; `include_steps(include_parameters=True)` also
loads step parameters; `include_resources()` loads assigned resources and
their child resources.

## Include archived runs and paginate

```python
runs = (
    query.process_runs()
    .include_archived()
    .order_by(Field("create_date").desc())
    .limit(25)
    .offset(50)
    .all()
)
```

Archived runs are excluded by default. `first()` is equivalent to applying
`limit(1)` and returning the first result.
